title: Compost banana peels
body: Chop peels into 2-3 cm pieces so they break down in 3-4 weeks. Bury under 5 cm of soil or add to a compost bin with dry leaves at a 1:2 wet:dry ratio to avoid odour and flies.

title: Citrus-vinegar surface cleaner
body: Pack peels into a jar, cover with white vinegar, seal 2 weeks, strain. Dilute 1:1 with water for a degreasing spray. Do not use on natural stone (etches marble/granite).

title: Reuse glass jars for dry storage
body: Soak off labels in warm soapy water, sterilise by boiling 10 minutes or oven-drying at 120C for 15 minutes. Use for pulses, spices, or leftovers. Discard jars with chips or cracks.

title: Self-watering plant spike
body: Pierce 3-4 small holes in the cap, fill the bottle with water, invert into the pot's soil. One 1L bottle waters a medium pot for 3-5 days. Use only bottles that held food or water.

title: Sheet-mulch weed barrier
body: Remove tape and staples, lay flat over weeds, wet thoroughly, cover with 5 cm compost or leaves. Suppresses weeds for a season and breaks down into the soil.

title: Repurpose a working phone
body: Factory-reset and remove the SIM/SD. A working phone can serve as a dashcam, a security camera (Alfred/IP Webcam), a music player, or an e-reader. If the battery is swollen, stop and route to e-waste.

title: E-waste must go to authorised recyclers
body: Under India's E-Waste (Management) Rules, electronics should be handed to a registered recycler or the brand's take-back. Never break boards open at home; the solder and coatings contain lead and brominated flame retardants.

title: Batteries are hazardous waste
body: Tape the terminals of loose batteries and drop them at a retailer or municipal battery-collection point. A swollen or leaking cell should be placed in a non-flammable container (sand/ceramic) and taken in promptly.

title: Cut worn cotton into cleaning cloths
body: Cotton and linen make good lint-free rags: cut into 30 cm squares, hem or pink the edges to slow fraying. Synthetic blends shed microfibres and are better donated or sent to textile recycling.

title: Never pour oil down the drain
body: Cooled used oil clogs pipes and sewers. Collect it in a sealable bottle; many Indian cities and RWACs run used-cooking-oil (UCO) collection for biodiesel. Small amounts can be soaked into paper and binned.

title: Safe kitchen scraps for cattle
body: Plain rotis, vegetable peels (potato, cucumber, gourd, carrot), and stale rice in small amounts are accepted by many gaushalas. Never give onion, garlic, avocado, chocolate, spoiled/mouldy food, or anything oily/spiced.

title: Household hazardous waste
body: Keep chemicals in their original labelled container. Do not mix products. Delhi residents can use MCD hazardous-waste collection days or authorised TSDF drop-off; check with your municipal ward office for the current schedule.
